candidates.summary: a merge-base render that failed is indistinguishable, in the posted comment, from a realm that had nothing to compare against
candidates.failure_scenario: renderBase (main.go:231-280) returns a nil *Crawler on five paths - empty -base-root, startGnodev error, waitReady timeout, base.Run error, base.Write error - each reporting to stderr only. ScreenshotPairs (shots.go:96) then leaves Before empty while New stays false, since newRealms only marks realms absent from baseRoot. pairGrid's `if p.Before == ""` branch renders the after shot alone with note == "", so the comment a reviewer reads carries the realm name, one image, and no word about the baseline. A reviewer approving a realm change on that comment believes the screenshot was compared against the merge base when nothing was rendered there.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./... -run 'B5Baseline|B5NewRealm' -v in misc/gnopreview at ecf7af0f2 with the artifact test: expect the comment to name the missing baseline, observe a body byte-identical to the New-realm body minus its <sub> note
candidates.evidence: Both tests PASS at ecf7af0f2. Body emitted for the failed-baseline plan: "### 🖼️ gnoweb preview **`gno.land/r/x/leaf`** **Changed realms (1)**" - no occurrence of before, merge base, baseline, compare or unavailable. TestB5NewRealmAndFailedBaselineAreTheSameMarkup passes, so strings.ReplaceAll(newRealm, " New in this PR — nothing to compare against.", "") == failedBase exactly.

candidates.summary: the indirect heading tells the reader a package changed when the only changed package is a realm
candidates.failure_scenario: indirect is every entry of p.Realms that is not a changed realm, but dependents() walks reverse imports of every changed pkg, realms included. A PR touching only gno.land/r/x/lib, imported by gno.land/r/x/app, leaves ChangedPkgs empty and p.Realms == [r/x/app, r/x/lib]; the comment then prints '**Realms affected through a changed package (1)**' and skips the `_changed:` line that would list the package, so the heading names a cause the PR does not have and the reader has nothing to reconcile it against.

candidates.summary: the index row guards only the realm link; the source and help links beside it are emitted whether or not those pages were captured
candidates.failure_scenario: Seeds() queues u, u+"$source" and u+"$help" per realm, and Run() skips any of the three on a transport error or a non-200 with a stderr line and a continue. So c.pages can hold /r/x/leaf while /r/x/leaf$help is absent, and Index still writes help. The reader of the published index clicks a 404 on a page whose sibling link was checked one expression earlier.

candidates.summary: sort.Strings(indirect) can never reorder anything; indirect is appended in the order of the already-sorted p.Realms
candidates.failure_scenario: plan.go sorts realms at line 259 and sorts plan.Realms again after the gnoweb seeds are appended, so every construction of p.Realms is sorted. indirect is built by a single forward range over it, and the sort is a no-op on every input the program can produce - a line that reads as a guarantee the caller already owns.
